sourceEval: evaluations/2026-09-24-remediation-gate.overloop.r1.json, re-read against the revised spec and the engine

improvementSurface: R1 the listing outcomes need the target's source and sink kinds, and a finding does not carry them
R2 pass 1's statement-removed says 'no sink of the target's kind in its program': a program with two such sinks, one fixed, reads gone-unexplained - G2.7 contradicts it
R3 pipeline step 9 resweeps a later revision; unrelated commits between fix and resweep would fail the verify on the added check
R4 'changed line' is used for both a deleted base line and an inserted head line without saying which each outcome means
R5 target.program is repository-chosen text and is not in repositoryText
R6 the gate needs the materialised trees after diff has compared them, and diffRefs removes them

measured.kindsResolve: 97 of 97 path rules in lib/sets/flow.mjs equal exactly one source-kind-to-sink-kind pair over the engine's 9 source and 22 sink kinds; no rule is ambiguous. The 3 other flow rules are construct (2) and context (1)

lowestDims.Robustness: still bounded by F1 until the listing outcomes are exact

improvements.change: a path rule's source and sink kinds are the one pair of the engine's kind tables its id spells; a test holds every path rule to exactly one pair, and a rule with none leaves the listing outcomes out, so it can only be gone-unexplained

statement-removed: the target's line is a deleted line and no sink of its kind in its program stands at an inserted line. source-removed: the same, for the source. The question is whether the patch wrote the statement back, not whether the program has another
improvements.blastRadius: decides pass for two of the three passing outcomes; G1.3, G1.5 and G2.7 exercise it

improvements.change: --target-only: only the target and coverage checks decide, for the resweep of a revision that holds other people's changes; the gate's own run keeps all seven
the spec says which side each outcome reads: a guard at an inserted head line; a statement or source at a deleted base line. repositoryText adds target.program

diffRefs is split into withRefs(repo, base, head, opts, fn), which materialises, calls fn with both roots, and removes them; diffRefs is withRefs with diffTrees, and diffTrees returns its two scans when asked
improvements.blastRadius: the hardened revision reader; test/diff-safety.test.mjs and test/review.test.mjs hold it, and diff's document must stay byte-identical

phase2_5_avoidanceAudit.note: the pass-1 fix I1 overcorrected; J2 is its correction, found by the pass-1 spec's own scenario G2.7

phase4_critique.why: without it the listing outcomes have no key
the pass-1 wording fails a scenario the same pass added
step 9 is half of what the command is for; without it every verify on a busy branch fails
phase4_critique.simpler: none: gating the fix commit against its parent covers only the merge, not a later resweep

phase4_critique.why: the gate cannot compute changed lines or compile without the trees
phase4_critique.migration: diffRefs keeps its signature and output

phase5_regressionsSet.togetherRisk: J5 changes the code path the diff-safety tests guard, and J2 decides passes; both carry tests that fail on the regression they could introduce
phase5_regressionsSet.ordering: J5 first (the gate needs the trees), then J1 and J2 (outcomes), then J3 (a mode over the checks)
phase5_regressionsSet.resourceConflicts: lib/diff.mjs: J5 only; lib/gate.mjs: J1, J2, J3
testGapsCreated: diff's document is unchanged after the split
every path rule resolves to one kind pair
--target-only ignores an added finding and still fails a still-reported target
phase5_regressionsSet.netDelta: about +50 lines of code; spec gains --target-only and a sharper §5

rescoreAfterBothPasses.note: the spec as it stands after both passes, before any code: dimensions that rest on implementation (Efficiency, Testability) move only when the tests exist
